# scratch-devcard — the live API

Everything here is READ FROM THE CODE at generation time. If this page
and the code disagree, the page is stale and the freshness gate
(`make -f renderer.mk scratchcard-brief`) is red.

The operational rule is `.claude/rules/scratch-devcard.md`; the task
playbook is the `scratch-devcard` skill. This page is the reference.

**A LIMIT WORTH KNOWING.** This rule is scoped to `tools/scratchcard/**`,
which covers the tool and the example an author copies. It does NOT
auto-load on a screen kept in gitignored scratch space — a `paths:` glob
matching zero TRACKED files can never fire, and the markdown gate refuses
one rather than let it look like coverage. Keep a screen you are iterating
on under `tools/scratchcard/example/`, or invoke the `scratch-devcard`
skill explicitly.

## Ops

Every op the daemon answers. Arg sets are CLOSED: an argument not listed here is REFUSED with `UNKNOWN_ARGUMENT` and the accepted set named, never silently dropped.

| op | accepted args |
|---|---|
| `diff` | `card`, `from`, `to` |
| `ping` | _none_ |
| `regenerate` | `bp-from-canvas?`, `card`, `families`, `file`, `keep`, `modes`, `resolutions`, `timeout-ms` |
| `status` | _none_ |
| `stop` | _none_ |

## Error codes

Typed, and CATEGORISED — a client-side code that collided with a daemon-side one would make a transport failure indistinguishable from a render failure.

| category | code |
|---|---|
| input (the screen file) | `INPUT_ASSET_MISSING` |
| input (the screen file) | `INPUT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` |
| input (the screen file) | `INPUT_COMPONENT_UNRESOLVED` |
| input (the screen file) | `INPUT_EXPAND_FAILED` |
| input (the screen file) | `INPUT_FONT_UNRESOLVED` |
| input (the screen file) | `INPUT_IR_INVALID` |
| input (the screen file) | `INPUT_MISSING` |
| input (the screen file) | `INPUT_READ_FAILED` |
| input (the screen file) | `INPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID` |
| input (the screen file) | `INPUT_SEMANTICS_INVALID` |
| render | `LANE_FAILED` |
| render | `RENDER_FAILED` |
| render | `RENDER_TIMEOUT` |
| render | `WRITE_FAILED` |
| protocol (the request itself) | `INVALID_CARD` |
| protocol (the request itself) | `MALFORMED_REQUEST` |
| protocol (the request itself) | `MISSING_OP` |
| protocol (the request itself) | `UNKNOWN_ARGUMENT` |
| protocol (the request itself) | `UNKNOWN_OP` |
| client-side (never sent by the daemon) | `DAEMON_DOWN` |
| client-side (never sent by the daemon) | `DAEMON_TIMEOUT` |
| client-side (never sent by the daemon) | `NO_RESPONSE` |
| client-side (never sent by the daemon) | `SPAWN_FAILED` |

## The run manifest — full schema

Written to `manifest.edn` in every run directory, VALIDATED on write and on read. The map is CLOSED: an unknown key is refused with the accepted set named.

```clojure
[:map
 {:closed true}
 [:run
  [:map
   {:closed true}
   [:id [:string {:min 1}]]
   [:utc [:string {:min 1}]]
   [:card [:string {:min 1}]]
   [:status [:enum :ok :error]]
   [:elapsed-ms [:maybe number?]]
   [:error
    {:optional true}
    [:map [:code [:string {:min 1}]] [:message string?]]]]]
 [:protogen [:map-of keyword? any?]]
 [:wasm [:map-of keyword? any?]]
 [:toolchain [:map-of keyword? any?]]
 [:protocol [:map-of keyword? any?]]
 [:host [:map-of keyword? any?]]
 [:matrix [:map-of keyword? any?]]
 [:input [:map-of keyword? any?]]
 [:lanes
  [:map
   {:closed true}
   [:producers [:sequential keyword?]]
   [:thresholds [:map-of keyword? any?]]
   [:caps [:map-of keyword? any?]]
   [:classes-sha [:string {:min 1}]]
   [:declined [:sequential keyword?]]]]
 [:renders
  [:sequential
   [:map
    {:closed true}
    [:cell [:string {:min 1}]]
    [:family [:enum 0 1 2]]
    [:dark [:enum 0 1]]
    [:w pos-int?]
    [:h pos-int?]
    [:bp [:int {:min 0, :max 3}]]
    [:disp-tier [:maybe [:string {:min 1}]]]
    [:status [:enum :ok :error]]
    [:fb-sha256 {:optional true} [:re #"[0-9a-f]{64}"]]
    [:png {:optional true} [:string {:min 1}]]
    [:dump {:optional true} [:string {:min 1}]]
    [:stats {:optional true} [:map-of keyword? any?]]
    [:error
     {:optional true}
     [:map [:code [:string {:min 1}]] [:message string?]]]]]]
 [:findings [:map-of keyword? any?]]]
```

## What judges a render

Read from `devcards.lanes` — this tool does NOT define its own quality rules.

- armed producers: `:tree-by-expect`, `:overlap`, `:deadzone`, `:opa`, `:emission`
- thresholds: `{:overlap/gap-px 0, :deadzone/gap-px 0}`
- caps: `{:vis-px? true}`
- DECLINED (named so silence is never mistaken for coverage): `:layers`, `:palette`, `:border`


## The default matrix

3 theme families x 2 modes x the canvases below = **42 cells**. The caller may override any axis.

| canvas | LVGL display tier | note |
|---|---|---|
| 1920x1080 | DISP_LARGE | 1080p |
| 1280x720 | DISP_LARGE |  |
| 1024x600 | DISP_LARGE |  |
| 800x480 | DISP_LARGE | the devcard corpus canvas |
| 640x480 | DISP_MEDIUM |  |
| 390x844 | DISP_LARGE | iPhone 13 portrait, logical pt |
| 844x390 | DISP_LARGE | iPhone 13 landscape |

The tier is a SILENT CLIFF: LVGL picks radius and padding from the greater axis (`<= 320` SMALL, `< 720` MEDIUM, else LARGE), so crossing a threshold changes geometry with no error. It is recorded per cell for that reason.

## A run directory

```text
.protogen/scratch/<card>/
  index.ednl        append-only roster, one EDN map per line
  latest -> runs/NNNN-…
  runs/NNNN-<utc>/
    manifest.edn     the machine-readable index — read this to diff
    report.md        the digest: verdict, grouped findings, what was NOT judged
    findings.edn     the FULL findings vector
    input/screen.edn a verbatim copy of what was rendered
    input/screen.pb  the bytes the renderer consumed
    renders/<cell>.png and <cell>.dump.json
```
